nodes.summary: For every field $F$, there is a real $k \ge 0$ at which the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ equals $2$. Hence the set of such $k$, viewed in $[0, \infty]$, whose supremum is the dual matrix multiplication exponent, is nonempty.
nodes.title: Some aspect has rectangular circuit exponent two

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $K \in [0, \infty]$. If $k \le K$ for every real $k \ge 0$ at which the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ equals $2$, then the dual matrix multiplication exponent $\alpha(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\alpha(F) \le K$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds for the dual circuit exponent

nodes.summary: For a field $F$, the dual matrix multiplication exponent $\alpha(F) \in [0, \infty]$ of the arithmetic-circuit model is the supremum of all real $k \ge 0$ at which the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ equals $2$.
nodes.title: Dual matrix multiplication exponent (arithmetic circuits)

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $k, w$ real numbers with $w > 0$. If the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ at aspect $k$ is less than $w$, then $w$ is an admissible exponent at aspect $k$ over $F$.
nodes.title: Exponents above the circuit exponent are admissible

nodes.summary: For every field $F$, the exponent $2$ is an admissible rectangular circuit exponent at aspect $0$ over $F$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ computes the product of an $n \times \lceil n^0 \rceil$ matrix and a $\lceil n^0 \rceil \times n$ matrix, that is of an $n \times 1$ matrix and a $1 \times n$…
nodes.title: Exponent two is admissible at aspect zero

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $k, w$ real numbers. The exponent $w$ is admissible at aspect $k$ over $F$ when $k \ge 0$, $w \ge 0$, and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ computes the product of an $n \times \lceil n^k \rceil$ matrix and an $\lceil n^k \rceil \times n$ matrix with at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$…
nodes.title: Admissible rectangular circuit exponents

nodes.summary: A circuit $c$ over a field $F$ whose inputs are the entries of an $m \times r$ matrix and an $r \times n$ matrix computes matrix multiplication when, for all matrices $A \in F^{m \times r}$ and $B \in F^{r \times n}$ and all $i < m$, $j < n$, its output at $(i, j)$ on the entries of $A$ and $B$ equals $(AB)_{ij}$.
nodes.title: Circuits that compute the matrix product

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $k \ge 0$ a real number. If the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ at aspect $k$ equals $2$, then $k \le \alpha(F)$, where $\alpha(F)$ is the dual matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model.
nodes.title: Aspects with circuit exponent two bound the dual exponent

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $k$ a real number and $W \in [0, \infty]$. If $W \le w$ for every real $w$ that is an admissible exponent at aspect $k$ over $F$, then $W$ is at most the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ at aspect $k$.
nodes.title: Lower bounds for the rectangular circuit exponent

nodes.summary: For a type $F$ of scalars and $m, r, n \in \mathbb{N}$, a matrix arithmetic circuit is an arithmetic circuit over $F$ whose inputs are indexed by the entries $(i, k)$ of an $m \times r$ matrix together with the entries $(k, j)$ of an $r \times n$ matrix, and whose outputs are indexed by the entries $(i, j)$ of an $m \times n$ matrix.
nodes.title: Matrix arithmetic circuit

nodes.summary: For matrices $A \in F^{m \times r}$ and $B \in F^{r \times n}$, the input assignment of $(A, B)$ is the function on the entry positions $(i, k)$ of an $m \times r$ matrix together with the entry positions $(k, j)$ of an $r \times n$ matrix that sends $(i, k)$ to $A_{ik}$ and $(k, j)$ to $B_{kj}$. It supplies the inputs of a matrix arithmetic circuit.
nodes.title: Matrix input assignment

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $k, w, w'$ real numbers with $w \le w'$. If $w$ is an admissible exponent at aspect $k$ over $F$, then so is $w'$.
nodes.title: Admissible circuit exponents are upward closed

nodes.summary: For every field $F$ and all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product matrix circuit over $F$ computes the product of an $m \times 1$ matrix and a $1 \times n$ matrix.
nodes.title: The outer-product matrix circuit computes the matrix product

nodes.summary: For every type $F$ of scalars and all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product matrix circuit over $F$ has exactly $mn$ gates.
nodes.title: Size of the outer-product matrix circuit

nodes.summary: For a type $F$ of scalars and $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product matrix circuit is the matrix arithmetic circuit for an $m \times 1$ matrix times a $1 \times n$ matrix with exactly $mn$ gates: for $i < m$ and $j < n$, the gate for $(i, j)$ multiplies the input at entry $(i, 0)$ of the first matrix by the input at entry $(0, j)$ of the second, and the output at $(i, j)$ is that gate.
nodes.title: Outer-product matrix circuit

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $c$ be a circuit over $F$ that computes the product of an $m \times r$ matrix and an $r \times n$ matrix, where $r \ge 1$. Then $c$ has at least $mn$ gates.
nodes.title: Lower bound for matrix multiplication circuits

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $c$ be a circuit over $F$ that computes the product of an $m \times r$ matrix and an $r \times n$ matrix, where $r \ge 1$. Then for all $i < m$ and $j < n$, the output of $c$ at $(i, j)$ is one of its gates, not a constant or an input.
nodes.title: Outputs of a matrix multiplication circuit are gates

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $k \ge 0$ a real number. If the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $\omega$ of the arithmetic-circuit model over $F$ at aspect $k$ is finite, then $\omega$ is itself an admissible exponent at aspect $k$ over $F$.
nodes.title: A finite rectangular circuit exponent is attained

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $k \ge 0$ and $w \ge 0$ be reals. The rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $k$ is at most $w$ if and only if $w$ is an admissible rectangular circuit exponent for $F$ at aspect $k$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ of size at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$ computes the product of an…
nodes.title: Upper bounds on the rectangular circuit exponent

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $k$ and $w$ be reals. If $w$ is an admissible rectangular circuit exponent for $F$ at aspect $k$, then the rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $k$ is at most $w$.
nodes.title: Admissible exponents bound the rectangular circuit exponent

nodes.summary: For every field $F$, the rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $0$ equals $2$.
nodes.title: The rectangular circuit exponent at aspect zero is two

nodes.summary: For a field $F$ and a real $k$, the rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $k$ is the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of the admissible rectangular circuit exponents for $F$ at aspect $k$: the reals $w \ge 0$ such that $k \ge 0$ and, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there are $C > 0$ and $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ of size at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$ computes the product…
nodes.title: Rectangular circuit exponent

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$ and every real $k$, the rounded inner dimension $\lceil n^k \rceil$ is positive.
nodes.title: The rounded inner dimension is positive

nodes.summary: For every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication circuit exponent of $F$ equals the rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $1$.
nodes.title: The square circuit exponent is the aspect-one rectangular exponent

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field with square matrix multiplication circuit exponent $\omega(F) \in [0, \infty]$, and let $w \ge 0$ be real. Then $\omega(F) \le w$ if and only if $F$ has rectangular circuit exponent $w$ at aspect $1$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ with at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$ gates computes…
nodes.title: Upper bounds on the square matrix multiplication circuit exponent

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field whose square matrix multiplication circuit exponent $\omega(F)$ is finite. Then $F$ has rectangular circuit exponent $\omega(F)$ at aspect $1$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ with at most $C n^{\omega(F) + \varepsilon}$ gates computes the product of every pair of $n \times n$…
nodes.title: The square matrix multiplication circuit exponent is attained

nodes.summary: For a field $F$, the square matrix multiplication circuit exponent of $F$ is the rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $1$. Since $\lceil n^1 \rceil = n$, it is the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of the reals $w \ge 0$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some arithmetic circuit over $F$ of size at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$ computes the product of…
nodes.title: Square matrix multiplication circuit exponent

nodes.summary: For every field $F$ and every real $k$, the rectangular circuit exponent of $F$ at aspect $k$ is at least $2$ (it may be $\infty$).
nodes.title: The rectangular circuit exponent is at least two

nodes.summary: For every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication circuit exponent of $F$ is at least $2$.
nodes.title: The square circuit exponent is at least two

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $k$ and $w$ be reals. If $w$ is an admissible rectangular circuit exponent for $F$ at aspect $k$, then $w \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Admissible rectangular circuit exponents are at least two
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
